chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from one who informed him, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man praying while a woman is praying beside him, he said: “There is no harm in it.”

So it is possible that what he عليه السلام intended was when there is more than ten cubits between the man and the woman, according to what ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī mentioned in his earlier narration; or that she is behind him. And it is possible that what is meant by it is when there is a barrier between him and her, according to what we mentioned in many reports, that the man places a screen between himself and her.

key_terms.بِحِذَائِهِ: beside him or parallel to him in position
key_terms.سَاتِرًا: a screen or covering placed as separation
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَذْرُعٍ: ten cubits, a measure of separation distance
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; no legal objection

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man and a woman praying beside each other in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage addresses the legal ruling of a man and woman praying in close proximity. It reports that there is no harm in such prayer, then explains that this is to be understood in light of other narrations: such as when sufficient distance exists, when the woman stands behind the man, or when a barrier separates them.
